source: PARTIAL SUPPORT; phenotype details still require species-matched confirmation. Partha et al. Rudiment with hidden function?, IOVS 31:1398-1404, PMID 2142147, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2142147/. Existing codes preserved, not blanket-approved.

basis_to_verify: eyes vestigial and covered by skin

Primary anatomical source located: Sweet G (1909), The Eyes of Chrysochloris hottentota and C. asiatica, Quarterly Journal of Microscopical Science 53:327-338, https://field.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/201079 (full original not inspected). Vestigial anatomy does not alone quantify residual photoreception. Fossoriality threshold still requires an explicit definition.

basis_to_verify: eyes minute and covered by skin or fused lids
source: REVIEW EYE_STATE 2; Grim N (1990), Whorl-Like Outer Segments in the Retina of the Mole (Scalopus aquaticus), Acta Anatomica 138:261-264, https://doi.org/10.1159/000146949; PMID 2389672. basis_to_verify: small eyes, poor vision; semi-aquatic foraging
source: MORPHOLOGICAL SUPPORT; Partha et al. (2017), eLife 6:e25884, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.25884: describes small eyes with thick eyelids and activity above and below ground. Its cited species source: Catania KC (1999), A nose that looks like a hand and acts like an eye: the unusual mechanosensory system of the star-nosed mole, J Comp Physiol A 185:367-372, PMID 10555270, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10555270/ (primary source located; eye-specific support taken from Partha introduction). Eye-state 1 is consistent with reduction, not proof of absent image formation. Review fossoriality 2 if defined as obligate subterranean rather than burrow-dwelling.

(2005), Features of visual function in the naked mole-rat Heterocephalus glaber, PMID 15647925, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15647925/: anatomical and physiological assays support small eyes and attenuated retinal responses. basis_to_verify: small eyes; retains visual function (treated as sighted in Extended Data Fig. 9)
source: DIRECT SPECIES-MATCHED ANATOMY; Herbin M, Reperant J, Cooper HM (1994), Visual system of the fossorial mole-lemmings, Ellobius talpinus and Ellobius lutescens, J Comp Neurol 346:253-275, https://doi.org/10.1002/cne.903460206; PMID 7962718. E. talpinus eye axial length 2.9 mm; reduced spatial resolution and retained central visual projections. Retain eye-state 1 as a provisional anatomical interpretation; do not recode to 0 for power and do not equate anatomical reduction with blindness. Existing Extended Data grouping is an analysis decision, not an independent phenotype source.

basis_to_verify: functional eyes; forages at the surface near burrow openings
source: DIRECT ECOLOGY ONLY; Lacey et al. (1997), Burrow Sharing by Colonial Tuco-Tucos (Ctenomys sociabilis), J Mammal 78:556-562, https://doi.org/10.2307/1382907: field capture/radiotelemetry supports residence in shared burrow systems. Does not validate eye-state 0, normal acuity, or the precise surface-foraging sentence. Related-species anatomy only: Vega-Zuniga et al. (2017), Selective binocular vision loss in two subterranean caviomorph rodents: Spalacopus cyanus and Ctenomys talarum, https://doi.org/10.1038/srep41704. C. talarum is not C. sociabilis; do not use as direct species validation. Eye-state 0 remains unverified; define whether occasional surface activity is allowed in fossoriality 2.

basis_to_verify: small eyes, functional vision in turbid water
source: SPECIES-MATCHED RETINAL SOURCE; Mass AM, Supin AYa (1989), Distribution of ganglion cells in the retina of an Amazon river dolphin Inia geoffrensis, Aquatic Mammals 15(2):49-56, https://www.aquaticmammalsjournal.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/12/Mass.pdf (publisher source located; full PDF access blocked). Author review: Mass and Supin (2007), Adaptive features of aquatic mammals eye, https://doi.org/10.1002/ar.20529, describes small eyes and retinal topography in Inia. Supports retained visual apparatus; eye-state 1 remains an interpretation requiring a comparative reduction criterion, not a blind state. A river dolphin is aquatic, not a terrestrial surface-dweller; fossoriality 0 must mean non-burrowing.

DIRECT RETINAL ANATOMY; Retina of river dolphin Lipotes Vexillifer (1983), PMID 6857230, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6857230/: reports an organised ten-layer retina and ganglion-cell organisation. Supports retained retinal structure; does not alone validate greatly reduced eyes, measured poor acuity or eye-state 1 against a specified comparator. Retain code as provisional until additional evidence and definitions are supplied. Fossoriality 0 must mean non-burrowing, not terrestrial surface habitat.

basis_to_verify: small eyes, poor vision; burrowing (sensitivity analysis only)
source: DIRECT BEHAVIOUR WITH LIMITATIONS; DiPaola JD, Yindee M, Plotnik JM (2020), Investigating the use of sensory information to detect and track prey by the Sunda pangolin (Manis javanica) with conservation in mind, Scientific Reports 10:9787, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-65898-x.
